priorStories.headline: Huawei convicted of fraud and trade-secret conspiracy
priorStories.body:
A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei on 10 criminal counts, including bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. The Justice Department said Huawei and three subsidiaries were convicted of offenses involving Iran sanctions, fraud and money laundering.

Jurors acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy. Sentencing remains pending, and a company attorney said Huawei would appeal the convictions.

sources.name: US Department of Justice via Forth

candidates.summary: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in Cartagena early November 25, ending a hostage siege that began the preceding day. President Abelardo de la Espriella said all remaining hostages were rescued and one captor was killed.
candidates.title: Colombian forces end Cartagena supermarket hostage siege

candidates.summary: Rescuers recovered three bodies on November 25 from an unauthorized gold mine in Bogor, West Java, and searched for 23 other miners believed trapped, AP reported. The flooding occurred late November 23 when heavy rain caused a nearby river to overflow into the shaft. Indonesia's search-and-rescue agency said the bodies were recovered shortly after midday local time; high water, narrow access and limited lighting complicated operations.
candidates.title: Three bodies recovered from flooded Indonesian gold mine

candidates.summary: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act on November 25, alongside an equity-financing fund that Reuters reported at €50 billion. The package seeks to strengthen European quantum technology and favour EU-controlled suppliers in relevant procurement, with exceptions for reciprocal partners. The legislation remains a proposal requiring negotiations with EU member countries and the European Parliament before it can become law.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes Quantum Act and technology equity fund
